# AGENTS.md — working on Black Hole

Instructions for any AI agent (or human) picking up this repository. Read this
first: the run is live, some of what you would normally do would break it.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **`huggingface-cli` is dead in this environment.** From `huggingface_hub`
> 1.x it prints usage help and downloads *nothing*, with exit code 0. Every
> download/login command in the docs uses **`hf download` / `hf login`** — if
> you find `huggingface-cli` anywhere (docs, scripts, your own muscle memory),
> replace it. Verified 2026-10-03.

* Project: **Black Hole** — decoder-only Transformer trained from scratch in
  PyTorch (no pretrained weights, no third-party model code).
* Reference docs: `README.md` / [French](README.fr.md) · `docs/`
  (ARCHITECTURE, TRAINING, DATA, EVALUATION, SFT, RECOVERY, MODEL_CARD,
  CHANGELOG).
* Hardware of record: one NVIDIA T4, 15 GB, 2 vCPU, 12 GB RAM — every number
  in this repo was produced there.

<!-- status:begin -->
> **live status** — step **25650/58000 (44.2 %)** · train **3.2280** (lr 1.949e-05) · val **3.8950 @ step 25500** · **bench 3.8651 @ 25500** (ppl 47.7) · pace **2.38 s/step → 21.4 h restantes**
>
> attention : `val` = éval du run (20 batches, sampler du run, step courant), `bench` = protocole fixe de `scripts/benchmark.py` (25 × 8 × 1024, seed 1234) étiqueté à **son** step — les deux diffèrent de quelques 1e-2 au même step.
>
> checkpoints locaux : `ckpt_step25000.pt`, `ckpt_step25500.pt` — sur le Hub : `ckpt_step24500.pt`, `ckpt_step25000.pt`, `ckpt_step25500.pt`
>
> courbes : `runs/bh-005/curve.png` (4 panneaux, dont la métrique secondaire raisonnement) · `runs/curve_benchmarks.png` (protocole officiel, tous les runs) — régénérées par `scripts/plot_curve.py`
>
> watchers : `train_watchdog.sh` (relance du trainer) + `keepalive.sh` (docs, push, benchmarks, supervision) + `watch_keepalive.sh` (relance du keepalive) — voir §2
>
> *généré le 2026-11-11 22:40 UTC par `scripts/sync_docs.py` — ne pas éditer à la main entre les marqueurs.*
<!-- status:end -->

---

## 0. Reprise de session — la checklist de l'agent qui arrive

> *« Tout doit être documenté pour qu'une session qui reprend sache tout. »*
> Cette section est le point d'entrée : elle tient en une page et elle
> renvoie à tout le reste.

| # | à faire | où | quoi exactement |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | lire l'état live | `AGENTS.md` (bloc `status:` ci-dessus) | step courant, LR, val, **bench officiel**, pace, ETA — chaque chiffre porte son step |
| 2 | lire le rapport de session | `runs/bh-005/SESSION_REPORT_2026-11-11.md` | ce qui a été fait, ce qui a été trouvé, ce qui reste ouvert |
| 3 | lire les règles | `AGENTS.md` §1 (règles d'or) et §6 (pièges déjà payés) | **ne jamais** toucher au trainer, **ne jamais** écrire un jeton dans un fichier |
| 4 | relancer la chaîne | `AGENTS.md` §2 | `train_watchdog.sh` (le trainer) **et** `watch_keepalive.sh` (le keepalive → le heartbeat → le dashboard) |
| 5 | vérifier que c'est live | `python3 -c "import json,time;d=json.load(open('runs/bh-005/live.json'));print(d['step'], int(time.time()-__import__('datetime').datetime.fromisoformat(d['updated_at']).timestamp()),'s')"` | l'âge doit être < 120 s ; sinon, le heartbeat est arrêté |
| 6 | vérifier la doc | `python scripts/audit_docs.py` | 13 contrôles : la documentation dit-elle encore vrai ? |
| 7 | suivre le run | `dashboard/` (local, port 3000) ou https://github.com/Ggboykxz/black-hole-dashboard | le dashboard live : courbe, GPU, bots, analyse, feuille de route, notifications |

**Ce qui existe maintenant** (aucun de ces éléments n'est à réinventer) :

| quoi | où | qui le produit |
|---|---|---|
| l'état live du run | `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `runs/bh-005/STATUS.md` | `scripts/sync_docs.py` (chaque cycle) |
| le registre des mesures | `docs/METRICS.md` | `scripts/metrics_ledger.py` (chaque cycle) |
| l'audit « la doc dit-elle vrai ? » | `runs/audit_status.json` | `scripts/audit_docs.py` (chaque cycle) |
| le heartbeat live | `runs/bh-005/live.json`, `Ggboykxz/black-hole-live` | `scripts/live_sync.py` (30 s) |
| l'instantané du dashboard | `dashboard/public/data/snapshot.json` | `scripts/dashboard_snapshot.py` (chaque cycle) |
| la copie GitHub du dashboard | `Ggboykxz/black-hole-dashboard` | `scripts/push_dashboard_github.py` (chaque cycle) |
| la feuille de route | `dashboard/app/roadmap` | dérivée des artefacts, jamais écrite à la main |
| les prédictions | `docs/PREDICTIONS.md` | écrites **avant** la mesure, jamais réécrites après |

---

## 1. Golden rules

1. **A run is in progress: do not disturb it.** Never `kill` the trainer, never
   fill the GPU, never restart the machine. Check first:
   `ps -eo pid,etime,cmd | grep -E "blackhole.train|train_watchdog|keepalive"`.
2. **Do not edit a running bash script.** Bash reads `scripts/*.sh`
   incrementally — rewriting one that is executing corrupts it. Kill the
   process first (by PID, see §5), edit, relaunch.
3. **Never `pkill -f <pattern>` where the pattern appears in your own command
   line** — it matches your shell and SIGTERMs you. Use
   `pgrep -f 'keepaliv[e].sh'` (bracket trick) or a PID you already know.
4. **GPU budget is 15 GB and the trainer holds ~10.2 GB.** Any experiment you
   run on `cuda` shares the rest; a short eval (25 × 8 × 1024, forward only)
   costs ~0.6 GB for 15 s and is safe. Anything heavier → run it on `cpu`, or
   you will OOM the trainer and lose up to `save_every` steps.
5. **`HF_TOKEN` only from the environment.** Never write it into a file, a
   config, a doc or a commit. The token in the chat history is fine-grained
   and should be revoked after the session.
6. **Documentation is generated, not hand-edited in the marked regions.**
   Everything between the `status:begin`/`status:end` markers (and the
   `benchmarks:begin`/`benchmarks:end` pair) is rewritten by
   `scripts/sync_docs.py` and `scripts/benchmark.py` — they locate the block
   by *literally* matching those markers, so never write the full HTML comment
   form of a marker anywhere else in a file. Edit *around* the blocks, then
   run both scripts.

## 2. The four background processes

**What to do while the run trains — and what to leave alone — is in
[`runs/bh-005/WHILE_RUNNING.md`](runs/bh-005/WHILE_RUNNING.md).** Short version:
CPU tasks under ~2 min are fine; the GPU and long CPU jobs wait.

| process | script | role | log |
|---|---|---|---|
| watchdog | `scripts/train_watchdog.sh` | starts/restarts training, `--resume auto` from the newest readable checkpoint, exits at `max_steps` | `runs/bh-005/watchdog.log` |
| trainer | `python3 -m blackhole.train` | the actual run | `runs/bh-005/train.log`, `log.jsonl` |
| keepalive | `scripts/keepalive.sh` | plots → samples → docs → ledger → **audit** → Hub push (**verified by SHA-256**) → checkpoint safety push → Hub pruning → benchmark → secondary metric → supervision, every `SYNC_INTERVAL` (300 s) | `runs/bh-005/keepalive.log` |
| keepalive-watchdog | `scripts/watch_keepalive.sh` | restarts the keepalive if its **pid file** (`runs/bh-005/keepalive.pid`) no longer names a live process, every `WATCH_INTERVAL` (60 s); exits at `max_steps` | same file, lines tagged `[watch]` |
| heartbeat | `scripts/live_sync.py` | publishes the **live** state of the run (log tail, GPU, processes, disk, last benchmarks) every 30 s to `Ggboykxz/black-hole-live` — this is what the dashboard follows when it runs on Vercel | `runs/bh-005/live.json` |

Start them (from the repository root, i.e. the `repo/` folder of the backup):

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
setsid nohup bash scripts/train_watchdog.sh configs/train-100m-bh005.json \
    >> runs/bh-005/watchdog.log 2>&1 &
SYNC_INTERVAL=300 CKPT_GRACE_S=300 WATCH_INTERVAL=60 \
    setsid nohup bash scripts/watch_keepalive.sh configs/train-100m-bh005.json \
    >> runs/bh-005/keepalive.log 2>&1 &
```

(`setsid` matters: a plain `&` dies with the shell that launched it, which is
how a keepalive silently disappears and the docs stop updating.

**After a Colab restart, this is the *only* gesture to do** — the watcher
starts the keepalive, which starts the 30 s heartbeat that feeds the live
dashboard (`docs/DASHBOARD.md` § « Reprise »). The dashboard's health panel
says so out loud if the chain did not come back: it shows the age of the
signal and the exact command to run. The first line
of `watch_keepalive.sh` does **not** start a keepalive itself — it starts one
within 60 s, from the pid-file check, so the log shows `[watch] ! keepalive
gone — starting it (restart #1)` on a fresh session. That is expected.)

If the watchdog died but training is fine, restart **only** the watchdog; if
everything is gone, `watch_keepalive.sh` restarts `keepalive.sh`, which restarts
the watchdog from the newest local checkpoint. The chain is
trainer ← watchdog ← keepalive ← keepalive-watchdog; each level only ever
restarts the one below it.

### 2.1 The autonomous driver — everything after step 8000

`scripts/next_phase.sh` chains the whole post-`bh-004` sequence in the
background, in order, with a marker file per stage
(`runs/_nextphase/<id>.done`) so killing and relaunching it resumes at the
first unfinished stage. Its log is `runs/_nextphase/driver.log`.

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...          # required, from the environment only (§1.5)
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD
bash scripts/next_phase.sh      # background; safe to relaunch after a crash
```

Stages: `wait_bh004` → `close_bh004` → `p1_gsm8k` → `export` → `sft1` →
`post_sft` → **`forget_gate`** → `tokenise` → **`preflight`** → `launch_bh005`
→ `supervise`.

Two design rules worth knowing:

* **critical vs. soft.** Measuring/building stages stop the driver on
  failure; publishing stages (`close_bh004`, `export`, `supervise`) only warn —
  a Hub push must never cost a training run.
* **the bold stages are measurement gates, not bookkeeping.** `forget_gate`
  refuses to continue when the post-SFT raw-text loss exceeds **4.20**
  (`docs/PREDICTIONS.md`, P4's falsification threshold), and `preflight` is the
  official `docs/TRAINING.md` preflight, which must confirm that
  `data/tokenized/val.bin` is still byte-identical to `bh-004`'s. If either
  says no, the driver stops and `bh-005` is **not** launched — that refusal is
  the point of the script.

During `supervise`, old `runs/bh-005/*.pt` are deleted from the Hub copy
(keep the 2 newest, ≈ 4 GB instead of ≈ 138 GB). The watchdog and keepalive
for `bh-005` are started by `launch_bh005` itself.

### 2.2 `scripts/push_loop.sh` — the orphan window

`keepalive.sh` is bound to a pretraining config and **exits when `max_steps`
is reached** — so when `bh-004` finished, the pusher went with it, and the
next keepalive only appears at `launch_bh005`. Without this loop the entire
post-8000 chain (GSM8K, SFT, tokenisation) would run with no push at all,
while it is exactly when new files are written.

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...
INTERVAL=300 bash scripts/push_loop.sh    # background, logs to runs/_nextphase/push.log
```

It pushes the working tree only (never `.pt`/`.bin`/`.parquet`), and **exits
by itself as soon as a real `keepalive.sh` is alive** — that is the handover
to `bh-005`'s supervision; two pushers racing on the same commit is how one
of them gets lost.

## 3. Day-to-day commands

```bash
python scripts/progress.py runs/bh-005      # step, ETA, val curve, checkpoints
tail -f runs/bh-005/train.log               # live console mirror
python scripts/test_docs_pipeline.py        # docs/figures/ledger/card pipeline: 33 checks, no GPU, temp tree
python scripts/sync_docs.py                 # refresh README/CHANGELOG/STATUS/AGENTS
python scripts/metrics_ledger.py --run runs/bh-005  # refresh docs/METRICS.md live block
python scripts/metrics_ledger.py --check            # exit 1 if a measurement drifted from the artefacts
python scripts/audit_docs.py --run runs/bh-005       # 12 claims (bench, P5, ledger, extractor, links) vs artefacts
python scripts/audit_docs.py --verbose              # same, printing the passing checks too
python scripts/dashboard_snapshot.py                 # refresh the dashboard's snapshot (dashboard/public/data/snapshot.json)
python scripts/live_sync.py                         # publish the live heartbeat (runs/<run>/live.json → Hub)
python scripts/push_dashboard_github.py              # commit + push the dashboard (snapshot included) to GitHub
python scripts/test_gsm8k_extraction.py             # the accuracy metric's extractor, on the 1319 real refs
python scripts/plot_curve.py runs/bh-005    # → curve.png (4 panneaux) + curve.md
python scripts/plot_curve.py --compare      # → runs/curve_benchmarks.png
python scripts/sample_progress.py           # 4 frozen prompts, CPU → runs/SAMPLES.md
python scripts/benchmark.py                 # measure the newest unmeasured ckpt
python scripts/eval_reasoning_val.py        # secondary loss, same windows (skips if its val.bin is absent)
scripts/rebuild_reasoning_val.sh            # rebuild that val.bin (gated, refuses during training)
python scripts/benchmark.py --report        # tables only
python scripts/backup.py                    # push code + docs + logs to the Hub
python scripts/next_reasoning.sh            # the P12/P13 pair (GPU — refuses to start while the trainer runs)
python scripts/verdict_reasoning.py         # read the two arms and say which lever it was
python -m blackhole.generate --weights runs/bh-005/ckpt_step12000.pt \
    --prompt "The history of the Internet" --max-new-tokens 60 --device cpu
python -m blackhole.evaluate --weights runs/bh-005/ckpt_step12000.pt \
    --data data/tokenized/val.bin --iters 25 --seed 1234 --device cuda --dtype fp16
```

Everything above is safe to run **while training**, except heavy `cuda` work
(rule 4). `scripts/progress.py` and `sync_docs.py` are read-only w.r.t. the
run.

Instruction tuning (see [`docs/SFT.md`](docs/SFT.md)): preparing the bins is
CPU-only and already done; the fine-tune needs the whole GPU **and** the
step-8000 checkpoint, so it waits for the end of `bh-004`.

```bash
python scripts/prepare_sft.py                   # Alpaca JSON → data/sft/ (done)
python scripts/prepare_sft.py --out data/sft-v2 \
    --cot data/sft_raw/gsm8k/main/train-00000-of-00001.parquet --cot-repeat 2
python -m blackhole.sft --init runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt \
    --data-dir data/sft-v2 --out runs/bh-004-sft   # after step 8000 only
python -m blackhole.evaluate --weights runs/bh-004-sft/best.pt \
    --data data/tokenized/val.bin --iters 25 --seed 1234 --device cuda --dtype fp16
python scripts/reasoning_eval.py --weights runs/bh-004-sft/best.pt \
    --device cuda --json-out runs/reasoning_eval.json   # the real number
```

**The improved fine-tune** (2026-11-10: replay + bucketing, 2.4× faster, and
the forgetting gate becomes a *search* over the checkpoints):

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...                    # the run pushes its checkpoints
scripts/sft_replay.sh                     # INIT/OUT/LR/EPOCHS/REPLAY_FRAC…
# then, instead of trusting best.pt:
python scripts/forget_sweep.py --dir runs/bh-004-sft-replay \
    --before runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt --threshold 4.20
# → runs/forget_sweep.json: the checkpoint with the lowest SFT loss among
#   those whose raw-text loss is ≤ the gate (the gate is a search, not a coin)
```

Two knobs that are **not** cosmetic:

* `--max-positions` (default 8 192) bounds the *padded positions* of a
  forward. The fp32 cross-entropy over 32 000 classes costs 4 bytes per
  position per class, so a 64-row batch padded to 512 tokens is 32 768
  positions ≈ 14 GiB of logits and gradients — an OOM on the T4. With
  length bucketing the batch is homogeneous, so the split adapts.
* `--replay-rows` (default 2) — the replay term carries a *loss weight* (5 %),
  not a share of the compute. The old default (8 rows × 1 024) made the raw
  text 74 % of the positions for 5 % of the gradient.

### 2.3 Generation speed — the Mercury 3 target

`blackhole/model.py` now has a **KV cache** and an opt-in **fast GQA**
(`model.set_fast_gqa(True)`). Both are checked, not assumed:

```bash
python scripts/test_kv_cache.py          # the generated ids are identical
python scripts/test_reasoning_cache.py --weights <ckpt> --limit 40
python scripts/bench_generation.py --weights runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt \
    --batches 1 8 32 64 --dtype fp16        # P9 — Mercury 3: 1 068 tok/s
python scripts/bench_generation.py --weights <ckpt> --mode reasoning \
    --batches 1 32 --dtype fp16              # P10 — the reasoning path
python scripts/bench_throughput.py          # the recipe of a 41 h run
```

* **Never** change what a published accuracy means: `--no-cache` reproduces
  the historical decoding, and the cache is proven text-identical.
* Every speed number carries its **batch, dtype and prompt length**.
* `torch.compile` stays off on 2 vCPU (the compilation cost is minutes); the
  measurement scripts say so rather than hiding it.

Reasoning — the GSM8K exact-match metric and the `bh-005` corpus
([`docs/EVALUATION.md`](docs/EVALUATION.md), [`docs/DATA.md`](docs/DATA.md)):

```bash
# smoke test — CPU only, safe while training (≈ 66 s/question here)
python scripts/reasoning_eval.py --weights runs/bh-004/ckpt_step4000.pt \
    --limit 8 --device cpu

# the full 1 319-question run — GPU, ONLY once the trainer has stopped
python scripts/reasoning_eval.py --weights runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt \
    --device cuda --json-out runs/reasoning_eval.json

# bh-005 corpus — steps 1-2 are network/IO, safe while training;
# step 3 (tokenisation, ~14 min CPU) competes with the dataloader → after bh-004
python scripts/render_reasoning.py             # → data/reasoning_raw/rendered.parquet
python -m blackhole.prepare_data \
    --shards data/reasoning_raw/rendered.parquet --out data/reasoning \
    --val-frac 0.02 --corpus-name numina-math-cot \
    --source https://huggingface.co/datasets/AI-MO/NuminaMath-CoT
cat data/tokenized/train.bin data/reasoning/train.bin \
    > data/tokenized/train_v2.bin              # then check, then launch
python -m blackhole.train --config configs/train-100m-bh005.json
```

The demo app lives in `space/` ([`space/README.md`](space/README.md)).
`selftest.py` is CPU-only and loads **no** weight → safe any time (13 s);
`python space/app.py` serves a Gradio UI on `http://127.0.0.1:7860` and *does*
read a checkpoint — run it only once the trainer is done (2 vCPU shared with
the dataloader). It resolves weights `WEIGHTS` → `exports/black-hole-100m-v2/`
→ most advanced `runs/*/ckpt_step*.pt` (now `runs/bh-005/`), on `cpu` unless
`DEVICE=cuda`.

```bash
python space/selftest.py               # template / imports / UI, no weights
python space/app.py                    # Gradio demo → http://127.0.0.1:7860
```

## 4. Conventions that make numbers comparable

| | |
|---|---|
| training seed | `1337` (torch / numpy / random) |
| evaluation seed | `1234` — same batches for every model |
| benchmark protocol | `val-25×8×1024-seed1234-fp16`, defined in `scripts/benchmark.py`, results in `runs/benchmarks.jsonl` + `runs/BENCHMARKS.md` |
| reasoning protocol | `gsm8k-test-1319-greedy-SFT-prompt`, defined in `scripts/reasoning_eval.py`, results in `runs/reasoning_eval.json` — **accuracy, never mixed with a loss column** ([`docs/EVALUATION.md`](docs/EVALUATION.md)) |
| LR schedule | warmup 200 → cosine to 1e-5 over 8000 steps (`blackhole/schedule.py`, single implementation); `bh-005` uses the same function with **58000** steps and peak **2.6e-5** — the seam LR is computed, not assumed (`docs/TRAINING.md`) |
| batch | 8 × grad-accum 4 × 1024 = 32 768 tokens/step, fp16 autocast + `GradScaler` |
| checkpoints | full state (weights + Adam + step + config), atomic write, pruned to the 2 most recent, pushed every 500 steps |
| SFT (instruction tuning) | one template `### Instruction:\n{instruction}[\n\n### Input:\n…]\n\n### Response:\n{output}<eos>` used for training *and* inference; data `yahma/alpaca-cleaned` → `data/sft/`, whole-example batches, lr 2e-5 — [`docs/SFT.md`](docs/SFT.md) |
| Hub layout | working tree → `repo/…`, checkpoints → `runs/bh-004/ckpt_stepN.pt` |
| model card data | `runs/baselines.json`, `runs/evals.json`, `runs/benchmarks.jsonl` |

`black-hole-tiny` has its own 516-token tokenizer and a 256 context: it is
scored on the same raw text re-encoded with its own tokenizer and flagged
`comparable: false`. Never put its perplexity in the same column as the 100 M
family without that caveat.

## 5. Resuming in a brand-new session

Follow `docs/RECOVERY.md` §1–2 verbatim: download `repo/` (code), `data/tokenized/*`
(1.4 GB — otherwise 44 min of re-tokenisation), and the newest
`runs/bh-004/*.pt`, copy the checkpoint into `runs/bh-004/`, then launch the
watchdog **and `watch_keepalive.sh`** (which starts the keepalive itself).
`--resume auto` walks `out_dir` from the newest checkpoint backwards
until one loads (weights **and** Adam moments), then falls back to
`extra.resume_fallback`; it never silently restarts from random weights.

Worst case for any single crash: **500 steps ≈ 17 min**, because
`save_every=500` is the real guarantee — not a signal handler.

## 6. Known traps (already hit, do not rediscover)

* **The SFT data was six pointers, not six files.** `data/sft*/train.bin`,
  `data/sft*/val.bin` and `data/sft_raw/alpaca_data_cleaned.json` were
  **133-byte Git-LFS pointers** in the working tree — *and on the Hub*, for
  weeks: the backup pushed the pointer, the pointer carried a plausible
  `oid sha256:`, and nothing looked wrong. The SFT phase (P6, P12 — the
  questions "does instruction tuning work at all") had **no data to train
  on**, and no document said so. The same scan found `data/tokenized/train.bin`,
  `data/tokenized/probe.bin` and `runs/bh-004/curve.png` as pointers.
  Restored byte-for-byte: the SFT bins were rebuilt from their sources
  (`yahma/alpaca-cleaned` + the GSM8K *train* parquet) and every rebuilt
  file's sha256 **equals the oid recorded in the pointer that replaced it**;
  `train.bin`/`probe.bin` were re-downloaded from the Hub (whose copies were
  real) and cross-checked the same way. `scripts/backup.py` now **refuses to
  publish a pointer** and names the files, and `scripts/audit_docs.py`
  checks it every cycle.
* **`huggingface-cli download` silently does nothing** (usage help, 0 files,
  exit 0) — use `hf download` / `hf login`. Found while auditing the runbook:
  a fresh session following the old `docs/RECOVERY.md` would have failed on
  its first command.
* **`--include "data/tokenized/*"` downloads 0 files, exit 0.** Every path in
  the dataset is prefixed with `repo/` (Hub layout, §4), so the pattern must be
  `"repo/data/tokenized/*"`. Found 2026-10-04 by following `docs/RECOVERY.md`
  §1 in a fresh session: the command "succeeds", the `mv` that follows fails,
  and the run then dies on a missing `train.bin`. `--dry-run` first — same
  trap family as `huggingface-cli` above.
* **The recovery download lands in `runs/hub/runs/…`, not `runs/bh-004/`.**
  Without the `cp` step of `docs/RECOVERY.md` §1, `--resume auto` finds no
  checkpoint and the `resume_fallback` file is missing too → training restarts
  from random weights *silently*. §1 ends with a pre-flight check; run it.
* **`AsyncPusher` swallows exceptions.** A failed checkpoint push only reaches
  `last_error`, printed at flush time; the log still says
  `↗ pushing … (background)`. This session's pushes were all failing on
  `from huggingface_hub import HfFolder` (removed in v1.x). Fixed in
  `blackhole/export.py`, and `scripts/keepalive.sh` now pushes any checkpoint
  missing from the Hub. If you touch `export.py`, run
  `python scripts/benchmark.py --report` and check `runs/bh-004/watchdog.log`.
* **The exporter used to write `runs/stepN/ckpt_stepN.pt`** while the docs
  (and keepalive) look for `runs/bh-004/…`. Both layouts exist on the Hub;
  keepalive accepts either, and the code now mirrors the local directory.
* **Two attempts share `log.jsonl`.** The GPU attempt that reached step 670
  without ever writing a checkpoint is archived in
  `runs/bh-004/attempts/gpu-510-670/`; the live log restarts at 510. Do not
  merge them — the weights of that attempt no longer exist.
* **`ckpt_step505/510` at the dataset root** are CPU continuations from a
  session without a GPU (see their `extra` field), not test fixtures.
* **2 vCPU**: `torch.compile` stays `false`, kernel-launch overhead is the
  bottleneck, and hashing 1.3 GB for an upload competes with the dataloader.
* **The T4 power-caps itself — plan against the *sustained* rate.** Cold, it
  does ~15,600 tok/s (2,09 s/step); after a few minutes of continuous load the
  card sits at 77 °C and 65–70 W of its 70 W limit, the driver reports throttle
  reason `0x4` (SW Power Cap) and the SM clock collapses to 465–1 020 MHz
  (≈600 average) → **~12,300 tok/s (2,66 s/step)**. GPU utilisation stays
  100 % and no other process holds VRAM, so this is the hardware and the
  Colab power budget, not the pipeline. Nothing was changed for it (the batch
  and the sequence length *are* the recipe) — but a session that plans its
  step count from a 10-step average taken at the start will over-promise by
  ~25 %.
* **`data/sft-v2`'s validation split leaks** — 306 of the 310 CoT validation
  examples (98,7 %) have an exact duplicate in train, because
  `prepare_sft.py` repeats the CoT examples *before* the split. Use
  **`data/sft-v3/`** (unique examples split first, CoT repeated train-side
  only, 0 leak, plus a held-out dev set). `data/sft-v2` stays for
  reproducibility only.
* **`data/tokenized/train_v2.bin` IS on the Hub** (3,83 GB,
  `repo/data/tokenized/train_v2.bin`) since 2026-11-10 — it was never pushed
  before, and rebuilding it costs 1 h 47 of tokenisation. `docs/RECOVERY.md`
  §1.1 has the one-command restore.

## 7. Definition of done — `bh-004`, then the reasoning phase

Items 1–7 close `bh-004` and its fine-tune. Items 8–11 are the reasoning
phase ([`docs/SFT.md`](docs/SFT.md), [`docs/DATA.md`](docs/DATA.md)).

The numbers these steps must hit are committed in
[`docs/PREDICTIONS.md`](docs/PREDICTIONS.md) (**P1–P7**) *before* being
observed. If one misses, it gets recorded as a miss there — not explained away
after the fact.

1. `summary.json` shows `step == 8000`, watchdog and keepalive have exited.
2. `python scripts/benchmark.py --all` + `--report`: the curve is complete and
   in `runs/BENCHMARKS.md`.
3. `python scripts/plot_curve.py runs/bh-004` → curve published.
4. Export and publish (`docs/RECOVERY.md` §5):
   `python -m blackhole.export --weights runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt … --push Ggboykxz/black-hole-100m-v2`.
5. `scripts/backup.py` one last time; update `docs/CHANGELOG.md`
   (the 0.3.0 entry is *in progress* until then) and the README status table.
6. Evaluate + sample the released weights, and record them in `runs/evals.json`
   / `runs/samples_baseline.json`.
7. Instruction tuning ([`docs/SFT.md`](docs/SFT.md)): `python -m blackhole.sft
   --init runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt --data-dir data/sft-v2 --out runs/bh-004-sft`
   (2 epochs ≈ 30 min on the T4), then the before/after perplexity on
   `data/tokenized/val.bin` recorded in `runs/evals.json` — the
   catastrophic-forgetting check — and the SFT checkpoint exported.
   *That is the command that was executed for `bh-004` (`data/sft-v2`, which
   leaks — §6). Every **new** fine-tune uses `data/sft-v3` (leak-free, with
   the dev hold-out), and P13's A/B uses `data/sft-v4`.*
8. **GSM8K baseline on `ckpt_step8000`**, GPU:
   `python scripts/reasoning_eval.py --weights runs/bh-004/ckpt_step8000.pt --device cuda`.
   This is *the* number the whole phase hangs on — the GRPO branch in the plan
   is conditional on it being ≥ 10 %. Record it whether it is good or not.
9. **GSM8K after the SFT of item 7**, same command, same seed → the delta is
   the first real measurement of whether the model can reason at all.
10. `bh-005` corpus built and verified: `data/reasoning/meta.json` exists with
    real (not projected) token counts, `data/tokenized/train_v2.bin` is the
    concatenation, and **`data/tokenized/val.bin` is byte-identical to
    `bh-004`'s** (checksum it) — otherwise the benchmark curve is void.
11. `bh-005` launched only after its preflight passes (`configs/train-100m-bh005.json`
    → `train_data` exists), and the same items 1–5 run against `runs/bh-005`.

## 8. Where the truth lives

| question | file |
|---|---|
| what step is it on? | `runs/bh-005/log.jsonl` (last line) — or `python scripts/progress.py` |
| is validation improving? | `runs/benchmarks.jsonl`, `runs/BENCHMARKS.md` |
| **does it actually solve problems?** | `runs/reasoning_eval.json` — accuracy, not loss |
| **what does it actually write?** | `runs/SAMPLES.md` — qualitative, greedy, never a metric (`scripts/sample_progress.py`) |
| **does any of it transfer?** | `runs/mceval.json` — 5 held-out MC sets, read `acc` against `baseline` (`docs/EVALUATION.md`) |
| **is the tail of the run still moving?** | `runs/soup_bh-005.json` — per-checkpoint drift ‖Δw‖/‖w‖ (1,42 % over 500 steps at 16 500→17 000); a soup that beats the last checkpoint means the basin is flat |
| **is the corpus actually clean?** | `runs/data_audit.json` — exact / prefix / near-duplicate rates (`docs/DATA.md`) |
| **what do we expect it to do?** | `docs/PREDICTIONS.md` — numbers written *before* the experiment, never edited after |
| **is this number comparable, and with what?** | `docs/METRICS.md` — registry M1–M14: definition, producer, artefact, step, comparability class, limits |
| **are the documented claims still true?** | `python scripts/audit_docs.py` → 12 checks: last benchmark in README/BENCHMARKS, P5 verdict, ledger block, GSM8K extractor, cited `runs/*.json`, doc links |
| **can I watch the run live?** | the dashboard (`dashboard/`, `docs/DASHBOARD.md`) — the live UI, deployable on Vercel; its data is produced by `scripts/dashboard_snapshot.py` + `scripts/live_sync.py`, never by the app itself. Published on GitHub: `Ggboykxz/black-hole-dashboard` (pushed by `scripts/push_dashboard_github.py`) |
| **what is the reasoning plan?** | `docs/TRAINING.md` (`bh-005`), `docs/DATA.md` (corpus), `docs/EVALUATION.md` (metric) |
| what was the last thing pushed? | `runs/bh-005/keepalive.log` |
| did the trainer restart? | `runs/bh-005/watchdog.log` |
| what is the plan? | `docs/TRAINING.md`, `docs/RECOVERY.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md` |
| **is the documentation internally consistent?** | `python scripts/check_links.py` → exit 0 = every intra/inter-doc anchor resolves |
| **do the figures and status blocks match the run?** | `python scripts/test_docs_pipeline.py` → 33 checks, no GPU, no network |
| what happened before? | `docs/CHANGELOG.md` + `runs/bh-004/attempts/README.md` |
prose.readme:
# Black Hole

A decoder-only Transformer language model **trained from scratch in PyTorch** — no
distillation, no pretrained weights, no third-party model code. The repository
holds everything needed to reproduce a run: model, tokenizer wrapper, data
pipeline, training loop, evaluation, generation and Hugging Face publishing.

* **Language:** English (this file) · [Français](README.fr.md)
* **Package:** `blackhole` (Python ≥ 3.10, PyTorch ≥ 2.1)
* **Hardware:** one NVIDIA T4 (15 GB) — every number in this repo was produced there

---

## Status

| Model | Layers × dim | Context | Vocab | Params | Loss (val) | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `black-hole-tiny` | 4 × 192 | 256 | 516 | 1.67 M | — | ✅ published 2026-09-30 |
| `black-hole-100m` | 12 × 768 | 1024 | 32000 | 100.09 M | 4.578 † | ✅ published 2026-09-30 |
| `black-hole-100m` @ step 500 (run `bh-003`) | 12 × 768 | 1024 | 32000 | 100.09 M | **4.522** † / **4.396** \* | ✅ checkpoint backed up |
<!-- status:begin -->
| `bh-005` — continuation → step 58000 | 12 × 768 | 1024 | 32000 | 100.09 M | 3.865 \* @25500 | 🔄 **step 25650/58000 (44.2 %)** — 2.38 s/step → 21.4 h left |
<!-- status:end -->

\* measured on `data/tokenized/val.bin` — the file the `bh-004` curve uses. The
`@N` suffix is the step that measurement belongs to (the State column shows
where training is *now*; the benchmark protocol only measures a checkpoint
every `save_every` steps).

‡ the run's *own* evaluation (`eval_every=250`, 20 batches, run sampler). The
primary number in the row is the **official benchmark**, always labelled with
the step it was measured at (`@16000`) even when training has moved past it;
the run evaluation is shown only if no benchmark exists at all. The two
protocols can differ by a few 1e-2 on the same step — the comparable series is
the one in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks--one-protocol-since-black-hole-tiny) /
[`runs/BENCHMARKS.md`](runs/BENCHMARKS.md). Definitions and limits:
[`docs/METRICS.md`](docs/METRICS.md).

† measured on `data/tokenized/probe.bin` (disjoint documents) — kept for
compatibility with the earlier runs. **The two are not comparable**: same
protocol (204 800 tokens, fixed batch seed, fp16), different documents — see
[`docs/EVALUATION.md`](docs/EVALUATION.md).

### What happened so far

1. **`bh-001` / `bh-002`** — the tiny model and the first 100 M run.
   `black-hole-100m` on the Hub is the export of `runs/hf/bh002.pt`.
2. **`bh-003`** — initialised from `bh002`, planned for 8 000 steps, interrupted
   at step 500 and backed up to
   [`Ggboykxz/black-hole-100m-backup`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ggboykxz/black-hole-100m-backup).
3. **`bh-004`** — resumed `bh-003` step 500 **with its Adam state**, on a fresh
   FineWeb corpus, to step 8 000: val **4.0083**, official benchmark
   **3.9441** (ppl 51.6) — done 2026-11-10.
4. **Instruction tuning (SFT)** — done on the leak-free `data/sft-v3/`
   (Alpaca + GSM8K chain-of-thought, 0 train∩val duplicate), with a replay
   term and the forgetting gate as a *sweep* over the checkpoints:
   `runs/bh-004-sft-replay/` (`best_val_loss` 2.2877) — [`docs/SFT.md`](docs/SFT.md).
   The full GSM8K **test** run (63–80 min on the T4) is still pending; only
   the 5-question smoke is recorded in `runs/reasoning_eval.json`.
5. **`bh-005`** *(this run)* — continued pretraining for 58 000 steps on
   **1 913 099 418 tokens**, 21.9 % of them worked derivations from
   [`AI-MO/NuminaMath-CoT`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AI-MO/NuminaMath-CoT).
   `val.bin` is **byte-identical** to `bh-004`'s (SHA-256 `673f8f97…`), so the
   official curve stays comparable with every number above; the reasoning

### Speed — the Mercury 3 target

The target set on 2026-11-10 is **Mercury 3** (Inception, 19/10/2026): a
frontier diffusion LLM whose headline number is **1 068 tokens/s**. Black Hole
cannot match its *quality* at 100 M parameters, but it can — and must — match
its *speed*: a decoder that re-reads its whole prefix at every token is not a
usable model, and that is exactly what `generate()` did before the KV cache.

<!-- speed:begin -->
| batch | dtype | prompt | new tokens | **tok/s** | vs Mercury 3 |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **39** | 0.04× |
| 8 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **459** | 0.43× |
| 32 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **1,892** | 1.77× |
| 64 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **3,060** | 2.87× |
| 1 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **62** | 0.06× |
| 8 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **477** | 0.45× |
| 32 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **1,839** | 1.72× |
| 64 | fp16 | 64 | 128 | **2,877** | 2.69× |
**Best: 3,060 tok/s at batch 64** — Mercury 3 (Inception, 19/10/2026) claims 1 068 tok/s. The KV cache and the fp16 weights are what make it possible: without the cache, decoding was O(T²).
<!-- speed:end -->

The cache is opt-in (`--no-cache` reproduces the historical path) and is
proven text-identical (`scripts/test_kv_cache.py`,
`scripts/test_reasoning_cache.py`).

## Crash recovery

A free Colab session can die at any moment, so the run is built to *restart*
rather than to *never stop*:

* **checkpoints are atomic** (`tmp` + `os.replace`) — a kill during the save
  can never leave a truncated file behind;
* `--resume auto` walks the run directory from the newest checkpoint backwards
  until one loads (weights **and** Adam moments), then falls back to the one
  named in the config; it never silently restarts from random weights;
* `scripts/train_watchdog.sh` restarts the process on any crash and forwards
  SIGTERM so a clean shutdown still saves;
* every checkpoint is pushed to the Hub asynchronously (`push_every=500`), so
  losing the VM costs **at most 17 minutes of training**;
* `scripts/backup.py` keeps the whole working tree (code, docs, logs) on the
  Hub, so a new session is back on its feet in minutes.

All of it is asserted by a test, not by hope:

```bash
HF_TOKEN=hf_... scripts/test_recovery.sh     # 11 assertions, ~2 min
```

It `kill -9`s a run mid-save, plants a truncated checkpoint and wipes the disk,
then checks that training continues at the exact step it stopped.
See [`docs/RECOVERY.md`](docs/RECOVERY.md) for the full runbook.

## Reproducibility

* **Seed** — `1337` (training), `1234` (evaluation batches). Same seed ⇒ same
  batches ⇒ comparable losses across runs and machines.
* **Schedule** — warmup 200 → cosine to `1e-5` @ 8 000 steps. Verified against
  the learning rate stored in the original checkpoint (`9.967408038682505e-05`
  at step 500 — exact match, see `blackhole/schedule.py`).
* **Checkpoints** — full state (`model` + `optimizer` + `step` + `config` +
  `tokenizer_path` + `extra`), fp32, written atomically, pruned to the two most
  recent, pushed to the Hub every 500 steps (asynchronous, ≈ 30 s).
* **Metrics** — every logged step is appended to `runs/<run>/log.jsonl`; the
  human-readable mirror is `train.log`.

## Loading a released model

```python
import json
from safetensors.torch import load_file
from blackhole.config import BlackHoleConfig
from blackhole.model import BlackHole

cfg = BlackHoleConfig.from_dict(json.load(open("config.json")))
model = BlackHole(cfg)
model.load_state_dict(load_file("model.safetensors"), strict=False)  # tied head omitted
model.eval()
```

# Changelog

All notable changes to the **Black Hole** model family and its training code.
Dates are UTC.

## Run — 2026-11-11 — la paire P12/P13 est prête à partir

* 🧪 **`scripts/next_reasoning.sh`** : le pilote de la **paire P12/P13**, la
  seule expérience qui répond à une question encore ouverte du dépôt
  (« le format `####` s'apprend-il par la perte ou par les données ? »).
  Il **refuse de démarrer tant que le trainer tourne** (le GPU appartient au
  run), chaque étape est marquée (`runs/_nextreasoning/<id>.done`) donc le
  pilote est idempotent, et la **porte d'oubli** (perte texte brut ≤ 4,20)
  est vérifiée **avant** les 1 319 questions — un bras cassé ne doit pas
  brûler une heure de GPU.
  * P12 : `data/sft-v3` + `--loss-on-response` (levier = la perte) ;
  * P13 : `data/sft-v4` (CoT up-weighté) + perte sur l'exemple entier
    (levier = les données) ; tout le reste identique, même décodeur, même
    graine 1234 que P1/P2/P11, et **les générations sont archivées** — donc
    re-scorables plus tard avec un meilleur extracteur (le piège qui pèse
    encore sur P1/P2/P11 ne pèsera pas sur celles-là).
* 🧾 **`scripts/verdict_reasoning.py`** : lit les deux bras et dit lequel a
  gagné, sans réécrire les prédictions (une prédiction se tranche, elle ne se
  réécrit pas) ; il écrit `runs/reasoning_verdict.json`.
* ✅ Vérifications du jour : `audit_docs.py` **13/13**, `check_links.py`
  98 liens / 0 cassé, `test_docs_pipeline.py` OK.
* ⚠️ `space/selftest.py` : 46/47 — seul l'échec est « import rapide < 15 s »
  mesuré à **47,5 s**. Ce n'est pas un défaut du code mais la **charge** de
  la machine (le trainer et le keepalive mangent les 2 vCPU) ; le même test
  passait à 13 s sur la boîte au repos. À rejouer quand le run s'arrête.

## Dashboard — 2026-11-11 — les cercles des bots sont expliqués, l'audit repasse à 13/13

* 🔍 **Les cercles autour des bots sont expliqués dans l'interface** : la
  grille porte une légende « les cercles » (anneau = l'état · arc = la mesure
  du bot · écran + emblème = l'acteur), chaque sprite a une infobulle qui le
  dit, et la légende de l'essaim le rappelle. Un cercle que personne ne sait
  lire est un cercle en personne ne doit pas faire confiance.
* ✅ **L'audit documentaire repasse à 13/13** : le test de l'extracteur GSM8K
  a été relancé sur les 1 319 références réelles (le parquet `main/test` a
  été retéléchargé — 419 Ko) et le bloc de mesure de `docs/METRICS.md` a
  été régénéré. L'extracteur redonne l'or sur 1 319/1 319 cas, et le repli
  « dernier nombre » en retrouve 1 283 (97,27 %) — la métrique M6 est
  citable.

## Dashboard — 2026-11-11 — avatars en 3D, le copilote devenu un personnage

* 🪐 **Les avatars sont en 3D** (CSS `perspective` + shading de sphère, sans
  dépendance) : l'orb du run est une planète qui tourne sur son axe — corps
  éclairé en haut à gauche, terminateur sombre en bas à droite, lumière
  rasante sur le bord, hotspot spéculaire — et les slimes des bots sont des
  boules de gel dont la lumière glisse quand on les attrape. Le halo d'état
  et l'arc de progression restent lisibles par-dessus.
* 🧑‍🎨 **Le copilote a un visage** : cheveux, sourcils, paupières (un vrai
  clignement), blush, et une **bouche qui bouge quand il parle** (enveloppe
  de syllabes, rythme ~120 ms). L'expression est un **état** : visite,
  pointage, alerte (le signal n'est pas live) ou concentration. Un geste
  (salut, hochement) ponctue l'accueil et les étapes de la visite.
* 🧠 **Le copilote se souvient** : dernière visite et nombre de visites sont
  persistés (`bh.copilot.v1`) et rappelés dans l'accueil — « je vous avais
  vu la dernière fois il y a 3 h 12 ».
* 🎀 **Un ruban de signal** en haut de chaque page : la couleur est l'état du
  signal (vert / ambre / rouge), lisible sans rien cliquer.
* 🐛 **Correction** : le registre des variations affichait la colonne VRAM
  avec l'index de la mauvaise métrique (l'utilisation GPU s'y glissait
  depuis le partage de la table des métriques) — les accès sont désormais
  nommés, plus indexés.
* ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` et `next build` passent ; instantané régénéré ;
  dashboard publié sur GitHub (`Ggboykxz/black-hole-dashboard`).

## Dashboard — 2026-11-11 — le bandeau est enfin live, et chaque changement est journalisé

* 🔴 **Le bandeau et le héros ne sont plus figés.** Ils étaient rendus par
  le serveur depuis l'instantané embarqué — un point vert « live » au-dessus
  de chiffres figés. Ils lisent maintenant le feed réel : l'état du signal
  (vert / ambre / rouge), la source, l'âge recalculé chaque seconde, le step,
  la perte, le LR, l'éval, le débit — et le **Δ exact** de chaque valeur qui
  bouge.
* 1️⃣ **Un seul poll pour tout le site** (`components/live-provider.tsx`) :
  le bandeau, le direct, les variations, les bots, la santé et les
  notifications lisent la même source. Trois polls concurrents ont disparu.
* 📜 **« Journal des changements »** (`/live`) : une ligne par valeur
  modifiée depuis l'ouverture de la page, à la précision du producteur
  (`perte train : 3,09412 → 3,08874 nats (−0,00538↓)`), avec l'origine
  (run / GPU / disque). Un onglet « mouvements » dans le centre de
  notifications, acquittable et persisté.
* 🎯 **Un échantillon par *mesure*, plus par poll.** La déduplication se fait
  sur la signature des valeurs : en local, l'API date sa réponse à l'instant
  de la lecture, donc deux polls identiques n'étaient pas deux mesures.
  Fini la ligne plate qui prétendait suivre.
* ⏱ **L'API locale date le signal de l'écriture du trainer** (`mtime` de
  `log.jsonl`) et non de la lecture : un trainer arrêté depuis 20 min ne peut
  plus passer pour « 0 s d'âge ». Cache-buster ajouté sur la lecture du
  heartbeat Hub.
* 🧩 **L'équipe de bots** : filtres d'état, jauges de progression,
  « depuis X » mesuré, **historique des transitions persisté** sur l'appareil
  (`localStorage`), sélection et filtre conservés au rechargement.
* 🌀 **Les avatars expliquent leur mouvement** : l'anneau du run tourne à la
  cadence mesurée, l'essaim est remué par l'activité réelle (changements/min,
  affichée dans la légende), le halo d'un bot porte son état. Avec
  `prefers-reduced-motion`, les créatures sont posées et ne bougent plus.
* ⌨️ **Copilote** : palette de commandes groupée et filtrable, navigation
  ↑/↓/⏎, anneau d'état, points de progression de la visite, bouton
  « repointer ».
* ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` et `next build` passent ; instantané régénéré ;
  dashboard publié sur GitHub (`Ggboykxz/black-hole-dashboard`).

## Dashboard — 2026-11-11 — le direct honnête, la traque des variations, le copilote incarné

* 🔴 **Un instantané n'est plus jamais servi comme du direct.** `/api/live`
  ne retombe plus sur `snapshot.json` : sans log local ni heartbeat, il
  renvoie **503** et l'interface affiche « aucune source live ». Un snapshot
  figé n'écrit **qu'un seul** échantillon, jamais un par poll — fini la

## 0.4.2 — 2026-11-10 — the speed target (Mercury 3), the gate as a sweep, and the SFT at 2.4×

**Target set by the user on 2026-11-10: Black Hole must reach the level of
Mercury 3** (Inception, 19/10/2026 — 1 068 tok/s, 1 M context, GPQA-D 89,2 %).
At 100 M parameters the *quality* of a frontier diffusion model is out of
reach (Chinchilla: ~2 G tokens puts a 100 M model around the GPT-2-small
class), so the reachable part of the target is the **speed** — and the speed
was, in fact, broken:

* ⚡ **KV cache in `blackhole/model.py`** — `generate()` re-read the *whole
  prefix* at every token: generating 192 tokens cost 192 full forwards over
  ~200 tokens, i.e. O(T²) instead of O(T). The cache (per-layer K/V, RoPE
  positions carried by `position_offset`, bottom-right-aligned causal mask
  when the query is shorter than the keys) makes decoding linear.
  `scripts/test_kv_cache.py` checks it the only way that counts: **the
  generated token ids are identical** (0 difference over 96 tokens), the
  cached next-token logits match a full forward to 2,6e-06, and the training
  path is untouched.
* ⚡ **GQA without materialisation** (`set_fast_gqa`, opt-in) — 12 query heads
  read 4 kv heads directly (`enable_gqa=True`) instead of repeating them 3×:
  ~600 MB of memory traffic saved *per generated token* at batch 32. Opt-in
  because it changes the rounding, and the benchmark series must stay
  comparable.
* 🆕 **`scripts/bench_generation.py`** — the Mercury 3 measurement (P9/P10):
  tokens/s by batch size, with the dtype, the prompt length and the cache on
  or off printed next to every number.
* 🆕 **`scripts/forget_sweep.py`** — the forgetting gate was binary and only
  looked at `best.pt`. Forgetting grows with the SFT steps, so the checkpoint
  that still predicts raw text is usually *not* the last one: the sweep
  measures **every** checkpoint of the run (raw-text loss = the gated metric,
  SFT loss = the optimised metric) and selects the best one that satisfies the
  gate. The gate becomes a search instead of a coin flip.
* 🆕 **`scripts/bench_throughput.py`** — the real optimizer step timed for
  several `batch × grad_accum` shapes, with peak VRAM, because `bh-005` is a
  41-hour run and the recipe must be chosen from a measurement.
* ⚡ **The replay term was eating the SFT** — the replay carries a *loss
  weight* (5 %), but the default gave it 8 rows × 1024 tokens per step: 74 %
  of the positions for 5 % of the gradient. `--replay-rows 2` gives the same
  8 192 replay tokens per step at a quarter of the cost, and `--grad-accum 2`
  halves the number of forwards: **2,60 → 1,09 s/step (2,4×)** — the
  fine-tune now takes 36 min instead of 78.
* ⚡ **Parallel tokenisation** (`prepare_data --workers N`) — the row groups
  of each shard are split between processes and concatenated in order, so the
  token stream is **byte-identical** (SHA-256 checked on a 20 000-document
  parquet: same `train.bin`, same `val.bin`) and the wall time drops: **164 s
  → 87 s** for 20 000 documents on a contended 2-vCPU box.
* 🐛 `sft.py` wrote a hard-coded `push_repo` in `train_config.json` — it now
  writes the value it was given (`""` means "no push", and the file said
  otherwise).
* 📄 `docs/PREDICTIONS.md`: **P9** (≥ 1 000 tok/s at batch 32, ≥ 250 tok/s at
  batch 1) and **P10** (≥ 1 000 tok/s on the *reasoning* path, with the
  accuracy protocol kept bit-comparable) were written **before** the
  measurement, with the two anti-cheating rules attached (the cache must not
  change the outputs; every speed number carries its batch, dtype and prompt
  length).
* 🔴 **`data/sft-v2`'s validation split leaked, and the previous SFT was
  selected on it.** `prepare_sft.py` repeats each GSM8K CoT example
  `--cot-repeat` times **before** the shuffle/split, so the two copies of an
  example could fall on opposite sides of the cut: measured on the bins,
  **306 of the 310 CoT validation examples (98.7 %)** — 306/1 310 = 23.4 % of
  the whole validation set — have an exact duplicate in train (Alpaca: 0 %).
  The SFT validation loss of `data/sft-v2` is therefore optimistic, and
  `runs/bh-004-sft-replay/best.pt` was chosen with it; that checkpoint is
  **provisional** until re-selected on a clean split. The GSM8K test number is

* 🆕 **`scripts/prepare_sft_clean.py` → `data/sft-v3`** — splits the **unique**

written, and P2 (GSM8K after the fine-tune) was never measured. This entry

and validated **on CPU while `bh-004` was still training** — the GPU was never
stolen from the run (rule 4 of `AGENTS.md`).

The plan, and the order is deliberate — measure before building, and **never
SFT before pretraining**:

1. ✅ exact-match harness (so nothing is claimed without a number),
2. ✅ one *mixed* Alpaca + CoT fine-tune (one pass of forgetting, not two),
3. ⏳ reasoning corpus **appended** to `train.bin` → `bh-005`,
4. ⏳ `bh-005` continued pretraining,
5. ⏳ GRPO, **conditional on the GSM8K base rate being ≥ 10 %**.

  tell you whether a model solves anything: `ckpt_step4000` sits at val loss
  4.04 and answers **0.00 % (0/5)** of GSM8K, writing the `####` marker 0 % of
  the time. That is the expected state of a pretrained-only model, and it is
  now a *recorded* baseline rather than an assumption.

  LR tail costs no training and asks a question a single trajectory cannot:
  is the model in a flat basin, or still walking downhill? The tool streams
  the checkpoints (≈ 1.7 GB peak RAM, not 5 × 1.3 GB) and **measures before
  building**:

  | | lr | drift vs. step 6000 |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | 6000 → 6500 | 2.38e-5 → 1.80e-5 | **+1.41 %** |
  | 7500 → 8000 | 1.09e-5 → 1.00e-5 | **+0.16 %** |
  | **end to end** | | **2.21 %** |

  The trajectory had nearly stopped (0.72 % over the last 500 steps alone),
  which is the *reason* to expect a soup to be neutral — and a soup that beats
  `ckpt_step8000` would instead mean the basin is flat and the run stopped
  early. Either outcome is worth having on record.

# Metrics — definitions, provenance and limits

This file is the **measurement ledger** of Black Hole. Its purpose is narrow
and strict: no number may circulate in the README, `AGENTS.md`, the changelog,
a status page or a model card unless it can be traced here to

1. a **definition** (what exactly is averaged, over which tokens),
2. a **producer** (the script and command that wrote it),
3. an **artefact** (the file on disk, with its checkpoint and step),
4. a **comparability class** (what it may and may not be compared with).

A loss is not an accuracy. A benchmark is not a capability. A point measured
before the gate is not the gate. Those distinctions are not pedantry: each one
has already produced a wrong sentence in this repository, and the ledger
exists so the next one is caught before publication.

The block delimited by the `metrics:` marker pair is generated by
`scripts/metrics_ledger.py` from the artefacts. The prose around it is
hand-written and changes only when a definition changes.

## 1. Rules

1. **One metric, one producer.** A published series has exactly one script
   that appends to it. `benchmarks.jsonl` is written only by
   `scripts/benchmark.py`; `reasoning_val_benchmarks.json` only by
   `scripts/eval_reasoning_val.py`; `reasoning_eval.json` only by
   `scripts/reasoning_eval.py`. A second producer would make the series
   uninterpretable even if the numbers agreed.
2. **Never mix protocols in one column.** The official web loss, the run's own
   validation loss, the secondary reasoning loss and GSM8K accuracy live in
   four different tables, even when they refer to the same checkpoint. A table
   may show them side by side only with an explicit protocol label.
3. **Every number carries its step.** A checkpoint is `ckpt_stepN.pt`, a
   measurement is `value @ step N`, and a status line that shows an older
   measurement says so. The live step and the measured step are different
   quantities.
4. **Never compare across files.** `probe.bin` (4 000 documents from shard
   `001`) and `val.bin` (the held-out tail of shard `000`) are different
   documents. A probe loss and a val loss are not comparable, even at the same
   precision and seed.
5. **Paired, not unpaired.** Comparisons at a fixed seed use the *same
   batches* for both models. Unpaired differences below ≈ 0.05 nats are noise;
   paired differences resolve ≈ 0.007 (`docs/EVALUATION.md`).
6. **Status is part of the number.** Every row in `docs/PREDICTIONS.md` is
   `MEASURED`, `PREDICTED`, `PROJECTED`, `REFUTED` or `PENDING`. A projection
   is never presented as a measurement, and a miss is recorded with the same
   prominence as a hit.
7. **Corrections append.** A published number is not edited to fit a later
   observation. A correction is a new dated row that explains the old one.
8. **A gate is settled at its own step.** P5 is the benchmark at step 16 000,
   not the first convenient point below 3.90. Intermediate points are
   evidence; only the named checkpoint fills the row.

## 2. Registry

| id | metric | definition | producer | artefact | comparability |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** | train loss | mean cross-entropy of the optimiser step, fp16 autocast, 8 × 4 × 1 024 tokens | `blackhole.train` | `runs/<run>/log.jsonl` | *within-run trend only* — the data stream and schedule differ between runs |
| **M2** | run validation loss | 20 batches, the run's own sampler, `eval_every = 250` | `blackhole.train` | `runs/<run>/log.jsonl` | *within-run trend only*; noisy (~±0.03 nats), **never** the published model-to-model number |
| **M3** | **official benchmark loss** | 25 × 8 × 1 024 = 204 800 tokens of `val.bin`, seed 1234, fp16, `model.eval()` | `scripts/benchmark.py` | `runs/benchmarks.jsonl` | **comparable across every 100 M run** — this is the primary series |
| **M4** | official perplexity | `exp(M3)` | `scripts/benchmark.py` | `runs/benchmarks.jsonl` | same as M3; a monotone transform, not independent evidence |
| **M5** | secondary reasoning loss | exactly the same 25 windows, but on `data/reasoning/val.bin` | `scripts/eval_reasoning_val.py` | `runs/reasoning_val_benchmarks.json` | **within-series only**; in-domain with the 21.9 % CoT training mix, **not** a transfer metric |
| **M6** | GSM8K exact match | fraction of the 1 319 test questions whose extracted final number equals the gold number; greedy, 192 new tokens, SFT prompt; **extractor v2** (2026-11-11), validated on the 1 319 real references | `scripts/reasoning_eval.py` | `runs/reasoning_eval.json` (+ `runs/reasoning_eval/<ckpt>.jsonl`, the raw generations) | **accuracy**, comparable only at n = 1 319; never mixed with a loss column. The three results published before 2026-11-11 used extractor v1 and did not archive their texts — see `docs/EVALUATION.md` |
| **M7** | `marker_rate` | fraction of GSM8K generations that contain the `####` convention *and* a number after it | `scripts/reasoning_eval.py` | `runs/reasoning_eval.json` | format compliance, **not** correctness |
| **M8** | generation throughput | tokens/s, measured with a fixed prompt length, dtype and batch size | `scripts/bench_generation.py` | `runs/generation_speed*.json` | only within the stated batch/dtype/prompt; batch 1 is launch-bound |
| **M9** | SFT validation loss | whole-example batches from `data/sft-v3/val.bin`, same template as inference | `blackhole.sft` | `runs/<sft-run>/log.jsonl` | model selection inside one SFT run; not comparable with M3 |
| **M10** | forgetting loss | M3 protocol applied to a post-SFT checkpoint on `val.bin` | `scripts/benchmark.py` / `runs/evals.json` | `runs/evals.json` | gate **≤ 4.20**; a raw-text loss, not an instruction-following score |
| **M11** | duplicate rates | exact / 100-char-prefix / MinHash-J≥0.5 rates over the reasoning corpus | `scripts/data_audit.py` | `runs/data_audit_reasoning.json` | data-quality diagnostic; a prefix rate is not a duplicate rate |
| **M12** | weight drift | `‖Δw‖ / ‖w‖` between the first checkpoint of the window and the last | `scripts/soup_eval.py` | `runs/soup_<run>.json` (`runs/soup_bh-005.json` for the live run, `runs/soup.json` for the historical `bh-004` window) | basin flatness, **not** quality. One 500-step window is a point, not a trend |
| **M13** | MC accuracy | accuracy on five held-out multiple-choice sets, log-likelihood of the continuation (`mc-ll-rank-v1`), read against the random-choice baseline | `scripts/mc_eval.py` | `runs/mceval.json` | transfer diagnostic; **absent** as of 2026-11-11 — the harness is validated (`runs/mceval_smoke.json`, 20 items, CPU) and the five datasets are cached locally, but the official numbers need the full sets on cuda/fp16; a subset, a CPU run or fp32 is recorded `comparable: false` with the reason |
| **M14** | probe loss | 25 × 8 × 1 024 on `probe.bin` | `blackhole.evaluate` | `runs/baselines.json` | legacy baseline only; **never** compare with M3 |

### What each metric does *not* say

* **M1/M2/M3/M5** say how well the model predicts the next token. They say
  nothing about whether a generated answer is correct.
* **M5** is measured on the same NuminaMath distribution that supplies 21.9 %
  of training tokens. A falling M5 is consistent with learning the *form* of
  worked derivations; it is not evidence of transfer.
* **M6** is the only registered capability metric, and it is exact-match on a
  single test set. It says nothing about open-ended writing, instruction
  following or calibration.
* **M7** measures formatting, not reasoning. A model can write `####` and be
  wrong; it can be right by the last-number fallback with `marker_rate = 0`.
* **M8** is hardware- and batch-dependent. "1 068 tok/s" without a batch size
  is not a measurement.
* **M10** is a *raw-text* loss. It detects catastrophic forgetting of web
  text; it does not measure whether instructions are followed.
* **M12** is a norm ratio. A flat basin is not automatically a good model.

## 3. Current run

`bh-005` is continued pretraining from `bh-004 @ step 8 000`, on
`data/tokenized/train_v2.bin`: **1 913 099 418 tokens**, of which
**419 651 726 (21.93 %)** are NuminaMath-CoT rendered twice. `val.bin` is
byte-identical to `bh-004`'s (`673f8f97…39cae`), so M3 stays comparable; the
reasoning domain is measured separately as M5.

Two token counts coexist here and must never be swapped:

* **step × 32 768** — what the *weights* have seen since the start of the
  lineage (`bh-003`, step 0), because the step counter is continuous across
  restarts and resumes. This is the number Chinchilla's 20 tokens/parameter is
  compared against (D2: ≈ 1.90 G at step 58 000).
* **(step − 8 000) × 32 768** — what *`bh-005` itself* consumed, since it
  resumed from `bh-004 @ step 8 000`. This is the budget of this run.

The generated block shows both, with the arithmetic in the source column.

The live values are in the generated block below. Two rules for reading it:

* `run val` and `bench` are different protocols. If both appear, the
  benchmark is the comparable one.
* The generated block may lag the live step by one benchmark cycle. It says
  which step each value belongs to; do not read a 15 500 measurement as a
  16 020 state.

![official protocol across runs](../runs/curve_benchmarks.png)

## 4. How to update

```bash
python scripts/metrics_ledger.py --run runs/bh-005   # rewrite the block
python scripts/metrics_ledger.py --check            # exit 1 if a measurement drifted
```

`--check` deliberately ignores the *live* rows (step, train loss, learning
rate, pace, tokens seen) and the generation timestamp: the trainer moves them
every ~20 s, so comparing them would make the check fail permanently and
therefore assert nothing. It compares the **measurement** material — the
official series, the paired web/reasoning series, the capability and gate
artefacts, the provenance and the known gaps — and fails when a producer has
written a point that the block does not show, or when a published value was
edited by hand. That is the drift worth catching; a block that is twenty steps
old is not drift, it is a block generated twenty steps ago.

`scripts/keepalive.sh` runs the writer every cycle, after
`scripts/sync_docs.py`, so the ledger cannot silently drift while a run is
live. If a producer changes its output schema, both the producer and this
ledger must change in the same commit.

The *other* direction is covered by `scripts/audit_docs.py`, also run every
cycle: it checks that the documented claims still match the artefacts (last
benchmark in `README.md`/`BENCHMARKS.md`, P5's verdict against the benchmark at
P5's step, this ledger's measurement block, the GSM8K extractor's own
validation artefact — including that it is *newer* than the extractor it
validates — every `runs/*.json` cited here, and the doc→ledger links). It is
offline, CPU-only and takes < 1 s.

```bash
python scripts/audit_docs.py            # exit 0 = all claims hold
python scripts/audit_docs.py --verbose  # print the passing ones too
```

# Predictions

Written **2026-10-04 19:08 UTC**, while `bh-004` was at **step 5600/8000** —
*before* any of the results in the table below were observed.

## Why this file exists

Every number this repository publishes is already measured after the fact. That
is the easy direction: given a curve, invent a story that fits it. It teaches
nothing, because a story that fits any outcome is falsified by none.

The hard direction is the only one that shows whether the chain — data →
pretraining → instruction tuning → evaluation — is actually *understood*:

> **write the number first. Then run the experiment.**

If the predictions hold, the model of the system in our heads matches the
system, and the next prediction can be trusted further. If they miss, the
interesting information is *in the miss*, and it arrives before the run costs
another 5 hours.

This is the whole difference between "we ran some scripts" and "we know what we
are doing".

## Rules

1. **A filled-in row is never edited.** A wrong prediction is corrected by
   appending a new row, never by rewriting the old one.
2. **Every prediction names the exact command and checkpoint that settles it.**
   A prediction nobody can check is a horoscope.
3. **A number, not a mood.** "I expect it to improve" is not a prediction.
4. **Misses are recorded with the same prominence as hits.**

tokens lands around the GPT-2-small class. What it *can* reach is the

not the arithmetic, is the limit.

So the target is written down here, in the project's own rules: **a number,
committed before the experiment.**

learned spontaneously, and the model's failure is *categorical* (0.0 %, not
"a bit less often") — which smells like dilution rather than like scarcity.
But this is a guess, and it is written down **before** the run so that it can
be wrong in public.

## What this baseline does *not* say

The `0.00 % (0/5)` figure quoted across the documentation is a **five-question
smoke test**. Its purpose was to prove the harness runs, not to measure
ability.

For 0 successes in 5 trials the exact (Clopper–Pearson) 95 % confidence
interval is **[0 %, 45 %]**. It is consistent with a model that solves nothing
*and* with one that solves nearly half of a small sample. The number that
actually settles the question is **P1**, at n = 1 319, where the interval
collapses to roughly ±0.5 pp.

Until P1 lands, "the baseline is 0 %" means *the harness works*, nothing more.

## Compute ceiling (measured)

Derived from the throughput above (14 421 tok/s for 100 M params) and from
Chinchilla's ~20 tokens/parameter.

| target | tokens | on this T4 | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **100 M compute-optimal** | 2.0 G | **38.5 h** (+33.5 h to go) | ✅ ~2-3 days of running |
| **300 M compute-optimal** | 6.0 G | **14.4 days** | ⚠️ possible if the box stays up |
| **1 B — first genuinely capable size** | 20.0 G | **160 days** | ❌ impossible here |

Memory, the harder wall. Full AdamW costs **16 bytes/parameter** (fp16 weights
+ fp32 master + two fp32 moments + fp16 gradients), against 5.07 GiB free:

| params | params+optimiser alone | fits in 15 GB? |
|---:|---:|---|
| 100 M | 1.6 GiB | ✅ (10.2 GiB total, observed) |
| 300 M | 4.8 GiB | ✅ ~13.4 GiB |
| 400 M | 6.4 GiB | ⚠️ ~15.0 GiB, no headroom |
| **1 B** | **16 GiB** | ❌ **weights and optimiser alone exceed the card** |

**Practical ceiling of this hardware: ~300 M parameters.** That is a fact
about memory, not about method — no amount of sequencing changes it.

## What "performant" can mean here

Three different claims, only two of which are available:

| sense | reachable? | price |
|---|---|---|
| ① **performant *for its size*** — beat comparably-sized public models on a fixed protocol | ✅ yes | ~33 h more tokens + the rest of the plan |
| ② **performant *absolutely*** — long reasoning, broad knowledge, useful autonomy | ❌ no, here | 160 days **and** 16 GiB |
| ③ **performant *as a system we understand*** — predict before observing | ✅ yes, this file | free |

The chronology in `TRAINING.md` and `SFT.md` is the same one any team would
run on 1 000 GPUs; only the scale differs. ① and ③ are what the current
budget buys, and they are worth building deliberately rather than by accident.

## What would falsify this plan

* **P4 fails** (loss > 4.20 after SFT) → the fine-tune is too aggressive; the
  learning rate or epoch count must come down before any reasoning work.
* **P6 ≤ 0** → the reasoning corpus in pretraining bought nothing, and the
  remaining effort belongs in data quality and SFT data, not more pretraining.
* **P1 > 5 %** → the pretrained model already generalises further than
  expected, and the reasoning story we are telling is understated — good news,
  but it means the 5 % anchor in P2 is wrong too.
* **the benchmark series stops improving before 3.90** → compute-optimal
  tokens (D2) matter more than everything else here, and D2 stops being
  optional.

## How to check

```bash
# what was predicted, and when
cat docs/PREDICTIONS.md

# the measurements that settle them
python scripts/reasoning_eval.py --weights <ckpt> --device cuda \
    --json-out runs/reasoning_eval.json
python scripts/benchmark.py --all --report
python scripts/progress.py runs/bh-004
```

Filled-in rows get their state changed from ⏳ to ✅ (hit) or ❌ (miss), with
the observed value written next to the prediction — never instead of it.

---

## Decisions — 2026-10-05 23:55 UTC
